channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Materiality
item.description: Themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. The Materiality call, guest curated by Francisco Gonzalez Camacho (@frangccom), seeks works that embrace a connection with the process and create a bridge between photography and other media — such as printmaking — to expand the capacities of the photographic form through alternative techniques, materials, and interventions. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with project description (max 500 words). Upload work to a public Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_ProjectTitle_01. Emails with attachments are deleted. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: THAT ONE PHOTOGRAPH · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Juried single-image call from Decagon Gallery for a photograph carrying emotional weight tied to memory, attachment, intimacy, grief, distance, tenderness, longing, or time. The brief favors images 'never fully left behind' over technical perfection. $1,000 total cash awards across five placements ($500 first plus solo website exhibition, $250 second, $150 third, two $50 honorable mentions). All selected photographers receive a dedicated exhibition page, Instagram feature, and catalog placement. Online exhibition July 1 – September 1, 2026. Open worldwide, all photographic styles and processes. — Deadline: June 20, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $1,000 total.

item.title: MUUS Collection Research Fellowship 2026
item.description: Inaugural research fellowship from the MUUS Collection, a New York-area photography archive holding nearly half a million images from the archives of André de Dienes, Fred W. McDarrah, Larry Fink, Rosalind Fox Solomon, Deborah Turbeville, and Alfred Wertheimer. $20,000 grant to one curator or academic to spend time in the archives and the new MUUSEUM Research Portal developing an exhibition or publication concept. Travel costs to the archive fully covered as part of the grant. Mentorship from an advisory board of leading curators and directors. Grant runs November 2026–November 2027. Winner announced at Paris Photo in October 2026. Open globally to curators and academics. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 + travel.

item.title: Jean Giono Photography Contest 2026 · Les Amis de Jean Giono
item.description: Free photography contest from the Friends of Jean Giono association, organised in partnership with Regards Alpins (a member association that runs photographic events tied to literature). Photographs — single image or coherent series — inspired by an excerpt from Giono's novel Noé, meditating on extraordinary landscapes and the act of seeing them through a lens. The 2026 Rencontres Giono festival is themed "Giono and Photography," running July 29–August 2 in Manosque; winners are announced at the festival on August 1, 2026. Open to amateurs and professionals of any age and country. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 / €300 / €200.

item.title: Guest Room: Annet Dekker & Margriet Schavemaker · Der Greif
item.description: Open call curated by Annet Dekker (Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis at the University of Amsterdam and co-director of the Centre for the Study of the Networked Image at London South Bank University) with Margriet Schavemaker (Director, Kunstmuseum Den Haag), exploring "The Brilliance of the Mundane." Invites reflections on the unnoticed and the unremarkable — images rooted in everyday life, shaped by happenstance, hasty habits, glitched files, accidental photos, and repetitive imagery — asking how to restore dignity to overlooked visual material and considering how these fragments operate as digital folklore fuelling contemporary image practices. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with a face-to-face feedback session from the curators. €250 Guest Room scholarship. Works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible. — Deadline: June 6, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: €250 scholarship.

item.title: Der Greif Issue 19 — I Am Because of You, Mother Earth · Der Greif
item.description: Open call for Der Greif's 19th print issue, guest-edited by Zanele Muholi — the South African visual activist and 2026 Hasselblad Award laureate, known for documenting Black LGBTQIA+ communities and reimagining Blackness. Theme: "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth" — examining environment as inseparable from bodies, histories, and relationships, with Muholi framing the body as a landscape, the face as geography, and breath as atmosphere. Accepts photography, writing, poetry, and essays from contributors worldwide; collaborative submissions encouraged. Selected work is reviewed by Muholi, published in Issue 19 with a free copy plus discounted additional copies, considered for an Artist Feature on dergreif.org, and may participate in Der Greif's Paris Photo 2026 events. — Deadline: June 20, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: Publication + Paris Photo 2026 events.

item.title: Fotografiska Emerging Portfolio Review 2026
item.description: Free open call for one-on-one online portfolio reviews with Fotografiska curators. Selected applicants receive a 20-minute review session on July 3, 2026 with Jessica Jarl (Global Director of Exhibitions, Stockholm) and Thomas Schäfer (Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska Berlin). Open to image-makers of all levels with a cohesive visual project. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Mrinalini Mukherjee Creative Arts Grant 2026 · Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation
item.description: Annual grant from the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation supporting innovative and experimental projects by established Indian artists. INR 10 lakhs (approximately USD 12,000) disbursed in two equal installments. Eligible disciplines span the visual arts including painting, sculpture, mural, textile, printmaking, performance art, and lens and media-based art. Open to Indian citizens currently residing in India with a minimum of 15 years of professional practice. Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and Persons of Indian Origin are not eligible. Individual artists and collectives may both apply. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $12,000 (INR 10 lakhs).

item.title: LUMINEX 4.0 · NOW Art
item.description: Fourth edition of LUMINEX, NOW Art's outdoor art and technology exhibition in Los Angeles. Open call for artists working at the intersection of art, light, and technology. Selected artists receive a $1,000 stipend plus production fees based on approved project. Free to apply. — Deadline: June 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 stipend.

item.title: SlowExposures 2026 — Photography of the Rural South
item.description: 20th annual Main Exhibition of contemporary photography of the American South. Submissions must be made in 16 Southern US states (AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, KY, LA, MD, MS, NC, OK, SC, TN, TX, VA, WV). Up to 6 images. Selected work shown September 18–20, 2026 at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in Concord, GA, then travels to Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, GA. Jurors Dennis Kiel and Coco Conroy. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Focus 2026 — Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: Open-themed juried exhibition for APG members based in Georgia. Juror Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director of the Houston Center for Photography. 2 to 8 images per entry. Exhibition runs July 21 – August 21, 2026 at the APG Gallery on Piedmont Avenue in Atlanta, with an opening reception July 23. The $1,000 APG/MOCA GA Purchase Award adds the winning work to the Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia's permanent collection. — Deadline: June 5, 2026. Fee: $35–$95 (members) / $30–$70 (students). Prize: $1,000.

item.title: America 250 — Photography Exhibition
item.description: Ninth national juried photography exhibition celebrating the U.S. Semiquincentennial. Open to USA artists 18+. Photography defined as digital or film camera work, unaltered except minor enhancements. AI-generated work not accepted. $800 in awards: $300 best capture of theme, $200 best traditional, $200 best non-traditional, $100 Award of Merit. Exhibition June 19 – August 1, 2026 at Gallery One in Ellensburg, WA. Jurors: Gail Gibson and C. Meier (Blue Sky Oregon Center for Photographic Arts). — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: $20 / $10 ea additional. Prize: $800 in cash awards.

item.title: Portal: At the Edge of Becoming · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Photographs that hold the viewer at the edge of something — work where a shift is imminent but not yet complete. Online curated exhibition with catalog inclusion and Instagram feature. First place receives $500 plus a solo webpage exhibition; second $300; third $200. Open worldwide, all photographic styles and processes welcome. — Deadline: June 3, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000 total + solo webpage.

item.title: A Celebration of Contemporary Photography · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: Open call celebrating the creativity, diversity, and evolving practice of photography today. Aligned with World Photography Day. Up to 35 images selected for the physical Middlebury, Vermont gallery and 40 for the online gallery, with all selected work appearing in the exhibition catalog and remaining permanently on the website. Open worldwide, all subjects, styles, and processes welcome. — Deadline: June 8, 2026. Fee: $39 / 5 images + $6 each. Prize: Gallery + online exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Future Photobook Award 2026 · Coventry University MA Photography & Fast Forward
item.description: Inaugural award for a photobook or photo-based publication (zine, handmade artist book, printed essay, etc.) by anyone over 18 currently studying at or recently graduated from a Higher Education institution. Winner receives personalised portfolio reviews with each judge plus an exhibition at a Coventry venue. All entrants receive feedback from industry professionals. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Portfolio reviews + exhibition.

item.title: Photoworks Artist Venturing Labs — EASE: Crete 2026–2027
item.description: Open call for a UK-based artist to join an art–science fieldwork lab in Crete in autumn 2026, exploring climate, landscape, and deep time alongside scientific teams. £1,000 stipend for the week on site; travel, accommodation, and meals fully covered. 24-month online engagement with EASE partners and Photoworks platform features. — Deadline: June 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 stipend + all expenses.

item.title: Circulation(s) Festival 2027 — 17th Edition Open Call
item.description: Annual open call for the festival of young European photography, held at CENTQUATRE-Paris and on tour across France and Europe. Now in its 17th edition (Spring 2027). Open to photographers of European nationality and/or resident in Europe at the start of their careers, with no age or training requirements. No theme — selection prioritizes aesthetic quality and artistic relevance. All forms of photographic writing welcome, including projects mixing formats or incorporating video, installation, or sound. Group projects accepted. Approximately 15 photographers selected for festival exhibition. AI-generated images must be disclosed. Selection by the Fetart collective (independent female curators specializing in emerging photography). — Deadline: June 7, 2026. Fee: Free until May 24 / €20 from May 25. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: Color 2026 · Grid Photo Gallery
item.description: International call exploring color as a central element of the image — as structure, signal, atmosphere, or disruption. Open to all photographic genres, methods, and subjects, provided color is integral to the image's internal logic. Selected work shown in curated online exhibition. First place receives Photographer of the Month feature with profile interview, priority promotional placement, and a free entry in the next open call. Second and third places highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries get permanent online display, social media promotion, digital certificate, and a profile page with website link. Selected works may also appear in a printed catalog. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: €7. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: F/262 Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Single-image international photography awards from the inaugural F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal (a UNESCO Creative City). Four award tracks: F/262 Photography Award (Gold/Silver/Bronze), ZÉ Creative Award, NextGen Award (emerging photographers), and the Thematic Award 'Moldar as Margens / Shaping Shores' tied to the festival's 2026 Water focus. Selected work is exhibited as outdoor public installations across the city during the festival (May 16 – September 13, 2026) and featured in the festival programme, press, and digital platforms. Gold winner receives a solo exhibition at F/262 2028, plus a €500 KOYLAB print voucher, BlackRapid Sport X strap, Outex Camera Pro Kit, and a 1-year SmartAlbums bundle. Silver and Bronze receive €400 and €300 vouchers respectively plus gear and software. Open globally; original work only; images must not have previously received a major international award. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €15/image. Prize: Exhibition + vouchers + 2028 solo show.

item.title: F/262 Photo Book Award 2026
item.description: Annual photobook award from F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal. Honors the best unpublished photobook project — 'from image to object, from story to print.' One author receives full local production of a 262-copy hand-numbered limited edition in Portugal, in collaboration with publishing partners and local craftspeople. Includes editorial and materials support, ISBN and colophon, launch event at the F/262 Photo Book Club, and international visibility through the festival programme. Open internationally; projects must be unpublished (self-published works of 100 copies or fewer are eligible). Collectives permitted; no entry limit per author (separate fees apply per project). Finalist dummy delivery due August 5, 2026 after July 1 application deadline. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: €35/project. Prize: Full photobook production (262-copy edition).

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Kazakhstan Residency 2026
item.description: Three-month fully funded residency at the Delfina Foundation in London for contemporary visual artists from Kazakhstan. Supported by SÄR Foundation as part of a five-year series of annual residencies for artists from Central Asia. Residency runs September 21 to December 11, 2026. Apply via Cognito Forms — read the Guidance Notes document before applying. — Deadline: June 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: SHOTS Magazine #172 — The Human Figure
item.description: Fall 2026 issue (#172) of the black & white photography quarterly, in print since 1986. Theme is the human figure — no need to be literal. Submit up to 8 grayscale images at 300ppi (color files converted to B&W upon receipt). Free for current/renewing subscribers; $25 for non-subscribers ($28 international). All processes, formats, and experience levels welcome. All submitting artists receive a complimentary copy of the issue. Initial selection by editor Elizabeth Flinsch. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free for subscribers / $25. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Drone Photo Awards 2026 · Siena Awards
item.description: International aerial photography contest run by Siena Awards (sister event to Siena International Photo Awards). Nine categories: seven single-shot themes (Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract, Sport), Videos, and Series (5–9 images). Drone Photographer of the Year receives the Pangea Prize crystal trophy, €500 worth of photography equipment, and €400 toward Siena travel for the Awards Ceremony weekend. Selected work shown in the "Above Us Only Sky" group exhibition. Awards ceremony at Teatro dei Rinnovati on October 10, 2026 during the Siena Awards Festival. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 gear + Pangea trophy + exhibition.

item.title: Collection 2026 - Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no limits. At least 26 images selected. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, museum-quality framing and matting handled by the gallery. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1–29, 2026 in Tucson, AZ. Juror: Holly Hart, Decode Gallery founder. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Art of Architecture
item.description: Virtual juried exhibition seeking architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, B&W or color, analog, digital or antique processes. Juror Michael Pannier (fine art photographer based in Greenville, SC) selects 35–40 images for the virtual gallery. Selected artists receive a portfolio review with the juror. 0% commission on sales. All photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: $35 / $28 members. Prize: Exhibition + Portfolio review.

item.title: Ethereal · A Photographer's Place
item.description: Seeking images that explore the intangible — works that evoke lightness, transience, and the space between what is seen and what is felt. Both traditional and experimental photographic processes welcome. Juror: John Horowitz, photographer and curator whose work resides in Purdue University's permanent collection. Exhibition June 5 – July 1, 2026 at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, NC. Opening reception June 5, 7–9 PM. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Critical Mass 2026 · Photolucida
item.description: Photolucida's annual program connecting photographers with the international photography community. Submit 10 images for pre-screening; approximately 200 finalists are then reviewed by up to 200 photography professionals worldwide — curators, gallerists, publishers, editors, educators, and media. The Top 50 are announced each year, alongside book awards and exhibition opportunities. Past finalists have gained acquisitions, exhibitions, and publication features. Open to photographers at any career stage. AI-generated imagery is not accepted for the 2026 cycle. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: $65 early bird / $75 regular; +$200 if Top 200 finalist. Prize: Top 50 designation + book/exhibition awards.

item.title: Immagini e trame d'acqua — Le Stanze della Fotografia Open Call
item.description: Inaugural open call from Fondazione Le Stanze della Fotografia (Venice) and the Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, gathering testimonies, stories, and reflections on water as a force and necessity within cultural and landscape heritage. The project starts from the UNESCO World Heritage Prosecco Hills but invites participants to explore the theme in relation to other heritage sites in Italy and worldwide. Two participation formats: a photography-and-text project (3–10 images plus a narrative text up to three pages) or a video-story (max 2 minutes combining images, words, and sound). Submissions made by email; participants must also publish their work on their own social channels tagging the promoters. Three awards per category — Best Visual Narrative, Best Language/Experimentation, and Special Mention for Under-30/Students. Selected works exhibited at Le Stanze della Fotografia and gathered in a brochure distributed at the foundation's bookshop. Open to citizens, students, photographers, videomakers, and storytelling enthusiasts of any age and nationality. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: EXPOSURE 2026 — 30th Annual Members' Juried Exhibition
item.description: Photographic Resource Center's 30th annual members' juried exhibition. Twelve photographers selected to exhibit three works each. Juried by Audrey Lee Sands, Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography at Harvard Art Museums. Exhibition runs July 31 – September 6, 2026 at University Hall, Lesley University in Cambridge, MA. Applicants must be PRC members through September. Awards: Juror's Choice Award ($200) and two PRC Choice Awards ($100 each). — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $400 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival 2026 Open Call
item.description: Open call for the 24th DongGang International Photo Festival, held July 17 – October 11, 2026 in Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: 'The Silence that Shapes' — exploring how humans interpret nature and what we project onto landscapes versus what nature actually reveals. 15–20 artists are selected by the festival's curatorial team, including one 'Artist of the Year' who receives a solo exhibition with production support and travel/accommodation to attend the opening. Other selected artists receive outdoor exhibition space, production assistance, and inclusion in the festival catalog and press. Open to individual artists and collectives worldwide. Submit 8–12 images (JPEG or TIFF, minimum 4000 px on long side) plus CV and an artist statement under 400 words by email or WeTransfer. Notification by June 10, 2026. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + travel/accommodation.

item.title: Vermont Center for Photography Artist Residency 2026
item.description: Inaugural artist residency at Vermont Center for Photography (VCP) in Brattleboro, VT. Two-week residency from October 23 to November 6, 2026. Open to photographers and lens-based artists at any career stage, working in analog, digital, or hybrid formats. Priority for artists who would benefit from darkroom and digital lab access, have a focused project proposal, and face barriers to creating elsewhere. Includes 24/7 access to VCP's darkroom, digital lab, and lighting studio; a $500 creation stipend; 14-night stay at the historic Latchis Hotel (4-minute walk from VCP); and a one-month solo exhibition in the Picker Print Gallery. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $25 ($15 members). Prize: $500 stipend + 14-night stay + solo exhibition.

item.title: Conversaciones — EMC Magazine Print Edition Open Call
item.description: Open call for the printed edition of Conversaciones, EMC Magazine's photography open call returning in a new format after three virtual editions. The editorial team seeks images that speak to each other. Free theme. Up to 5 images per participant, analog or digital, submitted via WeTransfer at low resolution for selection and high-resolution TIFF (300 dpi, RGB) if accepted. Open worldwide to photographers of any nationality. Selected participants receive one printed copy of the magazine; international participants cover shipping. Authors retain intellectual property; EMC Magazine receives non-exclusive usage rights for this printed edition. Publication planned for July 2026. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $5 USD / $5,000 ARS. Prize: Publication in printed magazine.

item.title: ESC 2036 — 0—1 Gallery Open Call · 0—1 Gallery
item.description: 0—1 Gallery's annual open call inviting artists to imagine roughly ten years ahead, keeping in mind the pressure points of now — climate, extraction, technology, and what it means to remain human inside all that. Looking for works that speak of nature, technology, or human existence — from subtle gestures to monumental systems. All forms welcome including photography, new media, painting, sculpture, installation, performance, sound, graphics, video, mixed media, AR/VR, and writing. No entry fees; submit one link to portfolio, website, or project page. Open to everyone — artists at any stage from any place; age, gender, location, and background not used as filters. Selected artists included in a curated group exhibition in the Netherlands in 2026–2027 with additional visibility through 0—1's website and social media. — Deadline: May 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Curated group exhibition.

item.title: Being Human — Artdoc Magazine Open Call · Artdoc Photography Magazine
item.description: Documentary photography open call inviting photographers to examine how human presence manifests in diverse cultural contexts. Portraits, environmental images, and documentary work — all approaches welcome. Selected work may be featured in curated online exhibitions, the Featured Submissions page, or upcoming magazine issues. Submissions free for Artdoc Magazine members; non-members must subscribe to submit. — Deadline: May 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication / online exhibition.

item.title: Flashes of Humanity — Pragovka Gallery 2027 Open Call
item.description: Open call for the 2027 exhibition program and International Residency Program at Pragovka Gallery, a contemporary art space in Prague. Theme: Flashes of Humanity / Záblesky lidskosti — what it means to be human today, including subtle, almost imperceptible moments such as brief encounters and small acts of attention. Personal experiences, social questions, and experimental approaches all welcome; no medium restrictions, photography eligible. Two tracks: (1) exhibition projects (authorial or curatorial) at Pragovka Gallery in 2027 with the gallery covering transport, installation, accommodation, travel by agreement, PR, documentation, printed materials, and artist fees; (2) residency projects in the International Residency Program with an 80 m² studio, accommodation, travel by agreement, artist fees, and material cost contributions. Open to Czech and international artists and curators. Submission deadline 11:59 PM on May 17, 2026. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition or residency at Pragovka Gallery.

item.title: Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant 2026–2027
item.description: Annual grant from the Stanley Greene Foundation providing a $10,000 award to emerging visual storytellers at the beginning of their careers to develop impactful visual narratives. The program places particular emphasis on photographers from underserved and diverse communities, expanding access to resources and opportunities to bring their stories to life. Award disbursed in two parts: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon submission of final materials. Application requires biography (max 1,500 characters), project description (max 2,000 characters), project proposal (max 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images (72 dpi JPG, minimum 1,500 pixels long dimension, sRGB). Submissions reviewed by three Foundation board members in two rounds. Recipients must provide 15 final digital images and a report detailing fund usage; these materials become part of the Foundation's collection. Open to applicants 18+; current students not eligible (graduating before announcement may apply). Honoring the legacy of war photographer and Noor Images co-founder Stanley Greene. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: Rencontres Marrakech + OFF Arles 2026 Open Call · Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech
item.description: 6th edition open call for the Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech and Festival OFF Arles 2026. Theme: 1826–2026: Two Centuries of Light, inviting work that explores light as origin, medium, language, and possibility — intimate or political, abstract or documentary, conceptual or experimental. 20 winners exhibit five photographs each at Galerie Triptyque in Arles during the opening week of Les Rencontres d'Arles (July 3–20, 2026), present a video at the Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech festival (October 7–10, 2026), and receive a dedicated online publication on the festival's official platform. 30 additional finalists also participate in the Marrakech video presentation and online publication. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Wassaic Project 2027 Artist Residency
item.description: 2–4 week residency at the Wassaic Project in the foothills of the Berkshires, two hours north of NYC. Summer sessions (3–4 weeks, June–September) take place in the Luther Barn studio building; winter sessions (2–4 weeks, January–March) in Maxon Mills. Open to individual artists, collaborative teams, and groups in any medium — photography eligible alongside painting, sculpture, installation, sound, video, and writing. Includes private bedroom in shared house, dedicated studio space (200–300 sq ft summer; ~100 sq ft winter), access to print shop and wood shop, studio visits with critics, and group programming. Need-blind sliding scale of $0–$900 per session covers most program costs. $25 application fee, waivable for hardship. Notifications by early October 2026. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: $25 (waivable). Prize: 2–4 week residency.

item.title: RAK Art Festival 2027 — Lost in Translation
item.description: 14th edition of the Ras Al Khaimah Art Festival, organized by the Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi Foundation for Policy Research at the Al Jazeera Al Hamra Heritage Village in the UAE. Theme: Lost in Translation — exploring displacement, migration, cultural adaptation, and the search for belonging across linguistic and cultural boundaries. Open to international artists across four categories: Emerging Artists, Established Artists, Filmmakers, and Students (ages 6–19). All nationalities welcome. Photography eligible alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, video art, and short film. Submit up to four artworks across two mediums maximum, with a 100-word artist statement and 200-word biography. Grand Jury Prize: AED 12,000 + trophy. Photography category prizes: AED 6,000 (1st) and AED 4,000 (2nd). Notifications: July 30, 2026; festival opens January 22, 2027. — Deadline: June 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: AED 12,000 grand prize + category awards.

item.title: FiiLTHY GLO Issue 5 — SONDER
item.description: Independent zine for the strange and unusual seeking work for Issue 5 — SONDER, exploring the intricately layered, sparsely noticed connections that intertwine us across society. Photography accepted alongside painting, collage, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, comic strips, prose, and short stories. Submit 1–5 original works related to the theme. Visual works should be cleanly presented (well-lit, minimal background); writing capped at 900 words per piece. Files named ArtistName_Title_Year. Submit via Google Form linked on the submissions page. — Deadline: June 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #138 — Documentary 2026
item.description: Documentary photography projects — work that focuses on recording events, environments, or everyday life in a straightforward, accurate way. Typically a longer-term focus than photojournalism, about a topic, place, or event. Submit up to 12 photographs with a project statement and/or descriptive captions. One submission per person. Published since 2004. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Life Framer — Street Life
item.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA). Theme: street photography, urbanscapes, observational moments, chance encounters. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Life Framer — Planet Earth
item.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Myrtille Delamarche (Editor-in-Chief, GEO Magazine). Theme: nature, landscapes, the planet's beauty and humanity's influence on it — landscapes, conceptual, aerial, documentary. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: XXIV Eurostars Grand Marina Photography Award — Josep Juanpere 2026
item.description: 24th edition of this international photography prize organized by Hotusa Group in Barcelona. 2026 theme: Barcelona, World Capital of Architecture, marking the city's UNESCO designation. Submit up to three photographic triptychs that form a cohesive visual narrative on the city's architectural identity. Named in memory of architect Josep Juanpere (1953–2025), designer of Hotel Grand Marina. First prize: €5,000 + trophy. Second prize: €3,000 + trophy. Eight finalists receive trophies and free stays at Eurostars hotels. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 (1st), €3,000 (2nd).

item.title: Headlands Center for the Arts AIR 2027
item.description: Fully sponsored 4–10 week Artist in Residence program at Headlands Center for the Arts in Sausalito, California. Approximately 60 artists selected each year, including local, national, and international applicants at all career stages. Photography is explicitly listed as an eligible discipline alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, film, video, new media, installation, writing, dance, music, interdisciplinary, social practice, arts professions, and architecture. Residency includes private studio space, chef-prepared meals, on-site housing, travel support, and a living expenses stipend. Application portal opens April 1, 2026; early bird fee ($35) closes May 4, 2026; regular fee ($45) thereafter. All applicants notified by December 11, 2026. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: $35 early bird; $45 regular. Prize: Fully sponsored 4–10 week residency.

item.title: Eliza Moore Fellowship for Artistic Excellence 2027 · Oak Spring Garden Foundation
item.description: Annual fellowship for one outstanding early-career artist developing new works that address plants, gardens, or landscapes in the broad sense. Open to visual artists (including photographers), literary artists, dancers, and musicians. Award includes a $10,000 individual grant and a required 2–5 week residency at the Oak Spring Garden Foundation's 700-acre estate in Upperville, Virginia, with access to staff, the rare book library (over 19,000 botanical art objects), and the working landscape. Eligible applicants must be early-career artists with some recognition through exhibitions, commissions, performances, grants, residencies, or publications, and not enrolled in an undergraduate program. Established artists with extensive solo exhibitions or published books are ineligible. 2027 residency start dates: March 1, April 25, May 24, July 12, August 29, or October 4. Application portal opens February 14, 2026. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 grant + 2–5 week residency.

item.title: Fondation Grantham Residency for Artists in Visual Arts 2027
item.description: Four-week residency with grant for established visual artists at Fondation Grantham, in the wooded francophone municipality of Saint-Edmond-de-Grantham, approximately 100 km east of Montreal. The Foundation supports projects whose subject matter, materials, or approach engage the aesthetic, social, and global implications of current environmental issues. Photography is explicitly included as an eligible practice alongside installation, sculpture, painting, graphic art, performance, and sound, digital, and media arts. Phase 1 grant of CAD $5,000 (residency, materials, and production); Phase 2 of up to CAD $5,000 to support continued project development. Travel allowance up to CAD $1,000 for artists residing 500+ km away. Open to artists from Quebec, elsewhere in Canada, or abroad with at least five years of professional practice; duos welcome. 2027 residency takes place in January, February, July, or August. Winners announced September 12, 2026. — Deadline: May 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: CAD $5,000–$10,000 grant + 4-week residency.

item.title: BLM Canyon Country District Artist in Residence 2026
item.description: Two- to four-week residency hosted by the BLM Canyon Country District in the Moab Field Office, Utah. Open to visual artists working in any medium suitable for digital reproduction, including photography, painting, printmaking, sculpture, and video. Selected artist creates work that represents the Canyon Country District; the BLM may suggest specific areas or themes within field office boundaries. Includes a $125/week stipend funded by the Canyonlands Natural History Association, access to a BLM campsite for the duration of the residency, and use of the Moab Field Office for drinking water and showers. Residency takes place between September 11 and October 31, 2026 (artist chooses dates and length). Selection panel includes BLM and Canyonlands Natural History Association staff who evaluate portfolio, resume, community engagement proposal, and application responses. Notifications by July 15, 2026. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2–4 week residency + $125/week stipend.

item.title: Sonntag Grant 2026 Photobook Open Call
item.description: Photobook open call from the Berlin-based Sonntag Grant for Photography in collaboration with Replika Publishing. Reserved for FLINTA artists (female, lesbian, inter, non-binary, trans, agender), 18+, of any nationality or location. Seeks projects that challenge the boundaries of the book as form, with emphasis on conceptual depth, material inquiry, and artistic dialogue. All forms of photographic work accepted; projects must be completed or at an advanced stage suitable for photobook production. AI-generated images are not accepted. One artist is selected to work directly with Replika Publishing to produce a new photobook with a print run of at least 350 copies (50 going to the artist). Submissions accepted globally from April 1 through midnight (Berlin/CET) on May 31, 2026. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: Photobook publication (350+ copies).

item.title: Ucross Spring 2027 Residency
item.description: Two- to six-week residency at the Ucross Foundation's 20,000-acre working ranch in northeastern Wyoming. Spring Session 2027 runs February through early June. Open to visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary artists, performance artists, and collaborative teams; both established and emerging artists encouraged, international applicants welcome. Approximately 115 residents per year; up to 10 in residence at any time. Includes living accommodations, all meals (chef-prepared lunch and dinner Monday–Friday, plus weekend provisions), dedicated work space, weekly housekeeping, linens and towels, and wireless internet. No stipend; residents provide their own materials and arrange travel to Sheridan, WY. Application opens May 1, 2026; no fee waivers available. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: 2–6 week residency.
